books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Thomas Nast, “The Union as It Was,” Harper’s Weekly, October 24, 1874; public domain.
stimulus.text: A Thomas Nast cartoon in Harper’s Weekly, October 24, 1874, shows two armed men shaking hands over a skull and crossbones above a cowering Black family. The man on the left carries a rifle and has “WHITE LEAGUE” on his pocket; the hooded man on the right wears “K.K.” on his robe. Behind them, a figure hangs from a tree and a schoolhouse burns. Above the scene an eagle carries the words “THIS IS A WHITE MAN’S GOVERNMENT,” and the caption reads: “THE UNION AS IT WAS. THE LOST CAUSE, WORSE THAN SLAVERY.”

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Thomas Nast, “The Union as It Was” (Harper’s Weekly, October 24, 1874), public domain
stem: This cartoon most directly reflects which development during Reconstruction?

options.text: Northern factory owners moving their businesses into Southern cities after the war to rebuild.
options.misconception: The cartoon shows armed Southern groups and a Black family, not Northern business owners.

options.text: The federal government building new schools for formerly enslaved children in the South after emancipation.
options.misconception: A schoolhouse burns in the cartoon; the scene shows schools under attack, not being built.

options.text: Southern states writing new constitutions that protected Black voting rights in 1868 for the first time.
options.misconception: The cartoon shows Black voters terrorized, not protected; the men shaking hands want the old order back.

options.text: White Southern groups using terror to restore white rule and undo the gains of Reconstruction.

rationales.A: No factory or business owner appears in the cartoon; the two men are armed Southern terror groups.
rationales.B: The burning schoolhouse shows education under attack, the opposite of the government building schools.
rationales.C: The cowering family and the hanging figure show Black rights under attack, not protected by new constitutions.
rationales.D: The White League man and the hooded Klansman shake hands over a skull above a frightened Black family, with a lynching and a burning schoolhouse behind them. Background: the Ku Klux Klan, founded in 1866, murdered and intimidated Black voters, and the period review names white Southern terror as one cause of Reconstruction’s failure.
rationales.general:
1. Name the two men. A White League rifleman and a hooded Klansman shake hands over a skull.
2. Look at who suffers. A Black family cowers below them while a figure hangs from a tree and a schoolhouse burns.
3. Read the eagle’s words. “This is a white man’s government” states the goal of the handshake.
4. Name the development. White Southern groups used terror to restore white rule and undo Reconstruction’s gains.
Remember: in a cartoon, the figures at the top show the power, and the figures at the bottom show who pays for it.
